items.markdown:
To make pour-over coffee, `use a 1:16 ratio of 20 grams of medium-fine coffee grounds to 320 grams of hot water heated to 205°F`.[[1]](https://pullandpourcoffee.com/how-to-make-pour-over-coffee/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)

### Equipment Needed

- **Pour-over cone** (like a Hario V60) and paper filters
- **Gooseneck kettle** for controlled pouring
- **Digital kitchen scale** 
- **Burr grinder** [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)[[2]](https://pullandpourcoffee.com/how-to-make-pour-over-coffee/)

### Step-by-Step Instructions

- **Rinse the filter:** Place your paper filter in the cone over your mug and wet it completely with hot water to remove any paper taste, then discard that rinse water.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)
- **Add the coffee:** Add 20 grams of freshly ground coffee (medium-fine, like sea salt) and shake gently to level the bed. Tare your scale to zero.[[1]](https://pullandpourcoffee.com/how-to-make-pour-over-coffee/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)
- **The bloom:** Pour 60 grams of hot water evenly over the grounds to saturate them. Wait 30 to 45 seconds to let trapped gases escape, which improves flavor.[[1]](https://pullandpourcoffee.com/how-to-make-pour-over-coffee/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)
- **First main pour:** Pour hot water in slow concentric circles until your scale reaches 190 grams. Wait a moment for the water level to drop slightly.[[1]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DFprrQqgy7x/?hl=en)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)
- **Final pour:** Pour the remaining water until the scale hits 320 grams. Let all the water drip through completely, aiming for a total brew time of about 2.5 to 3.5 minutes.[[1]](https://pullandpourcoffee.com/how-to-make-pour-over-coffee/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3TiNZXFIxNc)
